svg.title: Rossides's five-class model of the United States
svg.desc: Five horizontal bars sized by share of the U.S. population. Upper class, 1 to 2 percent: accumulate wealth and pass it to the next generation. Upper-middle class, 10 to 15 percent: doctors, lawyers, architects. Lower-middle class, 30 to 35 percent: teachers, nurses, small-business owners, clerical workers. Working class, 40 to 45 percent: manual, blue-collar jobs such as electricians. Lower class, 20 to 25 percent: lack both wealth and income and are politically weak.

text.font-family: Noto Sans, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: ROSSIDES’S FIVE-CLASS MODEL OF THE UNITED STATES
